overview: Kennack Sands is a gently sloping, sandy beach on the east side of the Lizard, about 500 metres long, backed by low cliffs and a little dune system. A rocky outcrop splits it into two halves, west and east, and the eastern beach is part of a nature reserve.

With lifeguards in season, parking and a café by the western end and toilets close by, it’s one of the easiest family beaches on the Lizard, and because it faces south-east it’s sheltered when the wind is from the west.

expect.title: Two beaches
expect.text: The rocks of the Caerverracks divide the beach in two; a path over Carn Kennack leads to the quieter eastern side.

expect.title: Tides
expect.text: Because the beach slopes so gently, the width of sand changes a lot with the tide.

expect.title: Diving
expect.text: Deep water close offshore makes it popular for launching dive boats.

goodToKnow.label: Facilities
goodToKnow.text: Parking and a café are at the western end of the beach.

goodToKnow.label: Where it is
goodToKnow.text: The nearest village is Kuggar, about a kilometre inland.

week.text: A reliable family beach day on the Lizard, especially when westerly winds make the other side of the peninsula wild. Combine it with Cadgwith for a wander and lunch.

pairWith.why: a working fishing village and cove nearby
an old stone works on the coast path

tips: Walk over the headland to the eastern beach for more space.
